clauses.原文: Identify the report as a systematic review in the title.
clauses.zh: 在标题中说明这是一篇系统评价。

clauses.原文: Describe the current state of knowledge and its uncertainties.
clauses.zh: 描述当前知识状态及其不确定之处。

clauses.原文: Provide an explicit statement of all objective(s) or question(s) the review addresses, expressed in terms of a relevant question formulation framework.
clauses.zh: 用某个提问框架明确写出本评价要回答的全部问题。

clauses.原文: use the Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome (PICO) framework or one of its variants
clauses.zh: 使用 PICO（人群—干预—对照—结局）框架或其变体。

clauses.原文: Specify all study characteristics used to decide whether a study was eligible for inclusion in the review
clauses.zh: 写明判定一项研究能否纳入的全部特征。

clauses.原文: Specify the date when each source (e.g. database, register, website, organisation) was last searched or consulted.
clauses.zh: 写明每个来源（数据库、注册库、网站、机构）最后一次检索或查阅的日期。

clauses.原文: Provide the full line by line search strategy as run in each database
clauses.zh: 给出每个数据库实际执行的逐行检索式。

clauses.原文: Report how many reviewers screened each record (title/abstract) and each report retrieved, whether multiple reviewers worked independently at each stage of screening or not
clauses.zh: 说明每条记录与每篇全文各由几名评价者筛选、各阶段是否独立双人。

clauses.原文: Report how many reviewers collected data from each report, whether multiple reviewers worked independently or not
clauses.zh: 说明每篇文献的数据由几名评价者提取、是否独立双人。

clauses.原文: Specify the tool(s) (and version) used to assess risk of bias in the included studies.
clauses.zh: 写明评价纳入研究偏倚风险所用的工具及其版本。

clauses.原文: Specify for each outcome (or type of outcome [e.g. binary, continuous]), the effect measure(s) (e.g. risk ratio, mean difference) used in the synthesis or presentation of results.
clauses.zh: 对每个结局（或结局类型）写明合成与呈现所用的效应量（如 RR、均数差）。

clauses.原文: reference the software, packages and version numbers used to implement synthesis methods
clauses.zh: 注明实现合成方法所用的软件、程序包与版本号。

clauses.原文: Specify the tool or system (and version) used to assess certainty (or confidence) in the body of evidence.
clauses.zh: 写明评定证据体确定性所用的工具或体系及其版本。

clauses.原文: Report the factors considered (e.g. precision of the effect estimate, consistency of findings across studies)
clauses.zh: 报告所考虑的因素（如效应估计的精确性、研究间结果的一致性）。

clauses.原文: Discuss any limitations of the evidence included in the review.
clauses.zh: 讨论纳入证据本身的局限。

clauses.原文: Discuss any limitations of the review processes used, and comment on the potential impact of each limitation.
clauses.zh: 讨论评价过程本身的局限，并说明每项局限的潜在影响。

clauses.原文: Provide registration information for the review, including register name and registration number, or state that the review was not registered.
clauses.zh: 给出注册信息（注册机构与注册号），或声明未注册。

clauses.原文: Report which of the following are publicly available: template data collection forms; data extracted from included studies; data used for all analyses;
clauses.zh: 说明哪些材料公开可得：数据提取表模板、从纳入研究中提取的数据、全部分析所用数据（原文此处被栏目标题「DATA, CODE, AND OTHER MATERIALS」截断，故条止于此；分析代码见下一条另计）

clauses.原文: Describe any methods used to assess certainty (or confidence) in the body of evidence for an outcome.
clauses.zh: 描述评定某结局证据体确定性（或可信度）所用的方法。

clauses.原文: Describe any methods used to assess risk of bias due to missing results in a synthesis (arising from reporting biases).
clauses.zh: 描述评估「结果缺失」所致偏倚（发表偏倚类）的方法。

clauses.原文: Describe the results of the search and selection process, from the number of records identified in the search to the number of studies included in the review
clauses.zh: 报告检索与筛选结果的全链条数字：从检出的记录数到最终纳入的研究数。

clauses.原文: The GRADE approach provides a transparent framework for assessing the certainty in evidence and for the development of recommendations according to transparently described criteria
clauses.zh: GRADE 提供的是一个透明框架：按公开写明的标准评定证据确定性，并据此形成推荐。

clauses.原文: be explicit about the certainty of the underlying evidence and how it links to the grade or strength of recommendations
clauses.zh: 明确写出证据确定性，以及它如何对应推荐的等级或强度。

clauses.原文: the PICO model (patient/population, interventions, comparators, outcomes)
clauses.zh: PICO 模型（人群／患者、干预、对照、结局）。

clauses.原文: be based on systematic reviews of the relevant evidence or on systematically and transparently extracted expert evidence if scientific evidence is missing
clauses.zh: 应基于相关证据的系统评价；确无科学证据时，才用系统、透明提取的专家证据。

clauses.原文: ROBIS risk of bias in systematic reviews
clauses.zh: ROBIS：系统评价的偏倚风险评价工具。

clauses.原文: Adolopment is a neologism referring to the systematic and transparent approach to adoption, adaptation and/or de novo development of recommendations to fit the context of interest.
clauses.zh: 「采纳—改编—新制」（adolopment）是一个合成词，指为适配本地情境，对推荐采取采纳、改编或重新制定的系统透明做法。

clauses.原文: There is no implementation without contextualization
clauses.zh: 没有本土化就没有落地实施。

clauses.原文: Trustworthy guidelines are the cornerstone of giving evidence-informed advice in response to clinical, public health and health policy questions.
clauses.zh: 可信的指南，是就临床、公共卫生与卫生政策问题给出循证建议的基石。

clauses.原文: Phase 2 aims to identify areas where bias may be introduced into the systematic review.

It involves the assessment of four domains to cover key review processes: study eligibility criteria; identification and selection of studies; data collection and study appraisal; and synthesis and findings.
Each domain comprises three sections: information used to support the judgment, signalling questions, and judgment of concern about risk of bias.
The domains should be considered sequentially and not assessed as stand-alone units.
The signalling questions are answered as “Yes”, “Probably Yes”, “Probably No”, “No” and “No Information”, with “Yes” indicating low concerns.

The subsequent level of concern about bias associated with each domain is then judged as “low,” “high,” or “unclear.” This rating was chosen rather than a rating of “Yes”, “No” or “Unclear”, because such a rating would either have meant that “Yes” was a bad thing in contrast to the phrasing of all signalling questions, or concern questions would have been worded awkwardly.
If the answers to all signalling questions for a domain are “Yes” or “Probably Yes”, then level of concern can be judged as low.
The first domain aims to assess whether primary study eligibility criteria were pre-specified, clear and appropriate to the review question.
This domain aims to assess whether any primary studies that would have met the inclusion criteria were not included in the review.
The third domain aims to assess whether bias may have been introduced through the data collection or risk of bias assessment processes.
The final phase considers whether the systematic review as a whole is at risk of bias.
The first signalling question for this phase asks whether the interpretation of findings addresses all of the concerns identified in domains 1 to 4.
ROBIS is designed to assess the risk of bias in reviews with questions relating to interventions, aetiology, diagnosis and prognosis.

GRADE is a system for assessing the quality of the evidence of each outcome in a review against eight criteria (including risk of bias, indirectness, inconsistency, imprecision, and publication bias).
In the GRADE system, the quality of evidence for each outcome is graded as HIGH, MODERATE, LOW or VERY LOW.
A HIGH rating means that, having assessed all of the potential problems with the evidence quality, we can be confident in our effect estimate.
Note that VERY LOW is the lowest quality rating, no matter how many reasons for downgrading quality there may be.
These assessments reflect the degree of confidence we can have in our effect estimate.
The GRADE system rates the quality of evidence for each outcome, from a rating of HIGH to VERY LOW.
There are several steps involved in moving from the risk of bias assessment for an individual study to a judgement about the overall risk of bias per outcome.
Effect measures can broadly be divided into ratio measures and difference measures (sometimes also called relative and absolute measures, respectively).
Risk ratios describe the multiplication of the risk that occurs with use of the experimental intervention.
Odds ratios, like odds, are more difficult to interpret (Sinclair and Bracken 1994, Sackett et al 1996).
The mean difference (MD, or more correctly, ʻdifference in meansʼ) is a standard statistic that measures the absolute difference between the mean value in two groups of a randomized trial.
RoB 2 is structured into a fixed set of domains of bias, focusing on different aspects of trial design, conduct and reporting.
Within each domain, a series of questions (ʻsignalling questionsʼ) aim to elicit information about features of the trial that are relevant to risk of bias.
Answers to signalling questions and judgements about risk of bias should be supported by written justifications.

The random-effects meta-analysis approach incorporates an assumption that the different studies are estimating different, yet related, intervention effects (DerSimonian and Laird 1986, Borenstein et al 2010).
A fixed-effect meta-analysis provides a result that may be viewed as a ʻtypical intervention effectʼ from the studies included in the analysis.
Subgroup analyses involve splitting all the participant data into subgroups, often in order to make comparisons between them.
Sensitivity analyses are sometimes confused with subgroup analysis.
Congruity between the stated philosophical perspective and the research methodology Does the report clearly state the philosophical or theoretical premises on which the study is based?
Congruity between the research methodology and the research question or objectives Is the study methodology appropriate for addressing the research question?
Congruity between the research methodology and the methods used to collect data Are the data collection methods appropriate to the methodology?
Congruity between the research methodology and the representation and analysis of data Are the data analyzed and represented in ways that are congruent with the stated methodological position?
Is the review question clearly and explicitly stated?
Critical appraisal or some similar assessment of the quality of the literature included in a systematic review is essential.
Ideally a review should present recommendations for policy and practice.
Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way?
Was appropriate statistical analysis used?
Searches should aim for high sensitivity, which may result in relatively low precision.
Search strategies should avoid using too many different search concepts but a wide variety of search terms should be combined with OR within each included concept.

Searches should capture as many studies as possible that meet the eligibility criteria, ensuring that relevant time periods and sources are covered and not restricted by language or publication status (see MECIR Box 4.3.a).
Searching beyond MEDLINE is important not only for ensuring that as many relevant studies as possible are identified, but also to minimize selection bias for those that are found.

第四条 伦理审查工作及相关人员应当遵守中华人民共和国宪法、法律和有关法规。

第十七条 涉及人的生命科学和医学研究应当具有科学价值和社会价值，不得违反国家相关法律法规，遵循国际公认的伦理准则，不得损害公共利益，并符合以下基本要求：
 （一）控制风险。

第十八条 涉及人的生命科学和医学研究的研究者在申请初始伦理审查时应当向伦理审查委员会提交下列材料：
 （一）研究材料诚信承诺书；
 （二）伦理审查申请表；
 （三）研究人员信息、研究所涉及的相关机构的合法资质证明以及研究经费来源说明；
 （四）研究方案、相关资料，包括文献综述、临床前研究和动物实验数据等资料；
 （五）知情同意书；
 （六）生物样本、信息数据的来源证明；
 （七）科学性论证意见；
 （八）利益冲突申明；
 （九）招募广告及其发布形式；
 （十）研究成果的发布形式说明；
 （十一）伦理审查委员会认为需要提交的其他相关材料。

第二十一条 伦理审查委员会批准研究的基本标准是：
 （一）研究具有科学价值和社会价值,不违反法律法规的规定，不损害公共利益；
 （二）研究参与者权利得到尊重，隐私权和个人信息得到保护；
 （三）研究方案科学；
 （四）研究参与者的纳入和排除的标准科学而公平；
 （五）风险受益比合理，风险最小化；
 （六）知情同意规范、有效；
 （七）研究机构和研究者能够胜任；
 （八）研究结果发布方式、内容、时间合理；
 （九）研究者遵守科研规范与诚信。
第二十五条 对已批准实施的研究，研究者应当按要求及时提交研究进展、严重不良事件，方案偏离、暂停、终止，研究完成等各类报告。
第三十三条 研究者开展研究前，应当获得研究参与者自愿签署的知情同意书。
第三十四条 研究参与者为无民事行为能力人或者限制民事行为能力人的，应当获得其监护人的书面知情同意。

第三十八条 研究过程中发生下列情形时，研究者应当再次获取研究参与者的知情同意：
 （一）与研究参与者相关的研究内容发生实质性变化的；
 （二）与研究相关的风险实质性提高或者增加的；
 （三）研究参与者民事行为能力等级提高的。
